title: Reproducing Gupta and Akhtar 2011: dry and wet oxidation of both faces of 4H-SiC, a second laboratory for Song's constants

sample.paper: “n-type 4H-SiC material … with maximum possible epitaxy layer (50 µm) on Si-face with lowest possible doping … CREE Research Inc. USA supplied the following structure on a 2” diameter wafer”
sample.note: Off-cut and doping value are in Figure 1(a), which has no text layer; not recorded.

sample.paper: “both faces of 4H-SiC”; which wafers carried the C face is not said
sample.note: With a 50 µm epilayer on the Si face, the C face is presumably the substrate side of the same wafers.

sample.ours: DOPING: n_type (recorded; no program reads it)

sample.note: Time from the HF dip to loading not stated.

sample.paper: “four numbers of samples were oxidized at same temperature for same oxidation time”

history.paper: “The wafers were treated for all three major chemical cleaning procedures i.e. Degreasing, RCA and Piranha.” … “Finally, the wafers were thoroughly rinsed in DI- water which, is followed by 10% HF dip.”
history.note: Every bath has its time (10 min each solvent, SC-1 10 min, HF 1 min, SC-2 10 min, piranha 15 min); the vocabulary's cleans are silicon cleans and none is this sequence.

history.paper: “The samples of each group were loaded and unloaded at 800C in the 1.9 LPM flow of nitrogen”
history.note: Push rate and time at 800 °C before the ramp are not stated.

history.paper: “the ramp up and ramp down temperature of furnace 5C/min as shown in figure 3”; the gas during the ramp is not stated
history.ours: RUN RampUp DURATION 4200 TEMP 800->1150 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: The rate is stated; nitrogen during the ramp is ours (the load is in nitrogen and the oxidizing gas is only said to flow during the process). A ramp in oxygen is a variant.

history.item: Oxygen at 1150 °C before the clock starts
history.paper: not stated: Figure 3 draws the oxidation time as the plateau only
history.ours: RUN BeforeClock DURATION 1 TEMP 1150->1150 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: An offset of time zero: oxygen reaching the sample before the plotted time begins (the gas switched on during the ramp's end, or a clock started late). 1 s, i.e. none, is the reproduction's value.

history.paper: “While in the experiment of dry oxidation, a continuous flow of constant dry oxygen is maintained throughout the process.” Times: Figure 10 axis 0.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 h
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 21600 TEMP 1150->1150 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Dry oxygen flow not stated. The text says 30 to 180 min in 30 min steps, Figure 3 says 0.5 to 6 h in 0.5 h steps, Figure 10 plots 0.5, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 h; Figure 16's t/X0 values fit Figure 10's times. Figure 10's times are used; the text's are a variant.

history.paper: “ramp down temperature of furnace 5C/min”; gas not stated
history.ours: RUN RampDown DURATION 4200 TEMP 1150->800 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: Nitrogen is ours. The curve points are taken at the end of the oxidation, so this step does not enter the scored numbers.

history.paper: “loaded and unloaded at 800C in the 1.9 LPM flow of nitrogen”

history.item: Thickness by ellipsometry, checked by stylus profiler
history.paper: “The thickness of thermally grown oxide on both terminating faces was experimentally captured by ellipsometry technique followed by DAKTEK surface profiler verification.”
history.note: Single-wavelength He-Ne ellipsometry. Four samples per condition, plotted “statistically”; no scatter given.
